<issue>
Super.getattr() method returns incorrect argument order

#### Description

When calling `getattr()` on a `Super` object, the method arguments are passed in the wrong order to the underlying `igetattr()` method, causing a `TypeError`.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
import astroid

code = '''
class A(object):
   test = 42
class Super(A, A):
   def __init__(self):
       super(Super, self) #@
'''

node = astroid.extract_node(code)
inferred = next(node.infer())
inferred.getattr('test')  # This should work but raises TypeError
```

The error occurs because `getattr()` calls `igetattr(context, name=name)` instead of `igetattr(name, context=context)`, mixing up the positional and keyword arguments.

This affects any code that tries to access attributes on super() objects through astroid's inference system.
</issue>
